cards.explanation: The answer is that they heard a bad report. The verse says Hamath and Arpad are put to shame “…for they have heard a bad report…” The report is the reason the verse gives. Some news lands harder than a dropped tray of cookies, friends.

The answer is that their anxiety cannot be calmed. The verse says they are “…agitated like the sea; their anxiety cannot be calmed.” Calm just won't come, friends. I've seen a mixing bowl settle faster than that.
The answer is False. The verse says “Damascus has become feeble; she has turned to flee.” Then it adds, “Panic has gripped her…” Fleeing is the opposite of standing your ground, friends.

The answer is that the LORD calls her a town that brings Him joy. Right in the middle of a hard message, He says, “How is the city of praise not forsaken, the town that brings Me joy?” That's a tender thing to say about a city. I think it's worth slowing down on that one, friends.

The answer is that they will be silenced. The verse says, “…all her warriors will be silenced in that day…” declares the LORD of Hosts. I think this one is heavy, so let's give it its weight. The LORD of Hosts is the one speaking.
The answer is fire. The LORD says, “I will set fire to the walls of Damascus; it will consume the fortresses of Ben-hadad.” Fire in my bakery is the oven's job, and it stays in the oven, friends.

The answer is Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The verse says Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor are the ones “…which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated…” Kedar is a desert tribe. Hazor comes up again in the very next verses, so keep that name handy, friends.

The answer is True. The verse says, “They will take their tents and flocks, their tent curtains and all their goods.” Tents and flocks are right at the front of the list. When your house is a tent, a lot of it can be carried off, friends.

The answer is that Nebuchadnezzar has a plan against them. The LORD says, “for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has drawn up a plan against you; he has devised a strategy against you.” That's the reason given. Right before it, the LORD tells Hazor, “Run! Escape quickly! Lie low…”

The answer is False. The LORD says of this nation at ease, “They have no gates or bars; they live alone.” It dwells securely, but no strong gates are named. Feeling relaxed and having defenses aren't the same thing, friends.
The answer is from all sides. The LORD says, “I will bring calamity on them from all sides…” The verse doesn't name one direction, friends. It says all sides.
The answer is a haunt for jackals. The LORD says, “Hazor will become a haunt for jackals, a desolation forever.” Then He adds, “No one will dwell there; no man will abide there.”

The answer is False. The LORD says, “No one will dwell there; no man will abide there.” He calls Hazor “…a desolation forever.” Elam's message later ends differently, friends, but this word about Hazor doesn't.

The answer is Elam's bow. The LORD of Hosts says, “Behold, I will shatter Elam’s bow, the mainstay of their might.” The bow is the thing Elam's might leans on, friends. And it's the very thing the LORD says He will shatter.

The answer is winds. The LORD says, “I will bring the four winds against Elam from the four corners of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds.” Then He says, “There will not be a nation to which Elam’s exiles will not go.”

The answer is False. The LORD says, “…I will scatter them to all these winds. There will not be a nation to which Elam’s exiles will not go.” They are spread out everywhere, friends. They don't gather in one far-off land.
The answer is True. The LORD says, “I will send out the sword after them until I finish them off.” I think this one is heavy, so I'll say it plainly and leave it there, friends.

The answer is His throne. The LORD says He will “…destroy its king and officials…” and in the same breath He says, “I will set My throne in Elam…” A throne is the seat of a king, so this is the LORD placing His own seat in Elam, friends.

The answer is a promise to restore Elam from captivity. The LORD says, “Yet in the last days, I will restore Elam from captivity…” After all those hard words, the last one is a promise, friends. And that little word “Yet” turns the whole thing.
